title: Build a useful practice round
use_when: The learner wants to practice, study, or be quizzed. Retrieve this guidance when choosing a practice approach.

rules.recommendation: Start with {value} clues when the learner does not specify a count.
rules.rationale: A short round leaves time to review mistakes before continuing.
rules.applies_when: The learner requests a practice round without a count.
exceptions: Honor an explicit count from 1 to 10; disclose when fewer matching clues exist.
rules.avoid: Filling a round with unrelated clues to meet the requested count.
rules.example_request: Give me a beginner practice round in Developer Tools.
rules.example_behavior: Recommend {value} clues, hide answers, and explain the short-round default.

rules.recommendation: Keep answers out of practice results; reveal a specific answer only when asked.
rules.rationale: The learner needs an opportunity to attempt the clue before seeing its answer.
exceptions: Use reveal_answer when the learner explicitly asks for an answer.
rules.avoid: Returning raw API search results that contain answers as a practice set.
rules.example_behavior: Return prompts and IDs; offer to reveal an answer after an attempt.

rules.recommendation: Use lower board values first for beginner practice and higher values first for advanced practice, while disclosing this rough proxy.
rules.rationale: Board value provides a reproducible ordering, but does not measure universal conceptual difficulty or the learner's knowledge.
rules.applies_when: Choosing a progression within the matching clues.
exceptions: Ask about the learner's topic or goal when they require conceptual difficulty; Final Jeopardy has no fixed board value and is placed last.
rules.avoid: Claiming that the highest-value clue is objectively the hardest for everyone.
rules.example_request: Find the objectively hardest material so I can master it.
rules.example_behavior: Explain the proxy's limit and ask which concepts the learner wants to improve.
